# #1793: Patch: the deck list marks each card that keeps the deck from being queued
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
Sometimes a deck can't be used: it holds a card the player doesn't own enough copies of, a card that was banned or retired, a token, or a custom card. The deck editor lists these problems as sentences above the deck, but the cards themselves look like every other card in the list. After importing a deck code, the player has to hunt for each named card among twenty-five tiles. Once built, each problem card in the deck list carries a warning mark and says what's wrong on hover and to a screen reader, the way a card shared with another deck already does.

## Why
- The validator's per-card errors already name the card: `LoadoutError.cardId` (`crates/engine/src/validator.rs:125`, `apps/web/src/wire/generated/LoadoutError.ts`).
- It is set by the L3, L5 (ownership), L6 and L7 rules (`validator.rs:323-461`).
- `DeckEditor.tsx:300` collects those `errors` and draws them only as text (`DeckEditor.tsx:474-484`, `data-card={issue.cardId}` on a list item).
- `DeckTile` (`DeckSidebar.tsx:96-157`) takes only `conflict`. Its flag, `title` and `aria-label` exist only for a card that is also in another deck.
- The pool side already marks unowned cards (`PoolGrid.tsx:169`, `data-owned`), so the deck side is the odd one out.

## Proposal
- In `DeckEditor`, build a map from card id to the first error naming that card, and pass it to `DeckSidebar`.
- `DeckTile` sets `data-issue={rule}`, adds the error's translated message to its `title` and `aria-label`, and shows the existing `db-tile-flag` mark in a warning tone.
- Errors without a card id stay in the verdict box only.

The client decides nothing new. It shows the verdict the engine's validator already gave (CLAUDE.md rule 7).

## Where it lands
- `apps/web/src/game/deckbuilder/DeckEditor.tsx`, `DeckSidebar.tsx`, `deckbuilder.css`
- `apps/web/src/game/deckbuilder/DeckWorkshop.test.tsx`
- §9.4's loadout rules, read and not changed. No spec change.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] In a deck with a card the collection owns none of, that card's tile has `data-issue="L5"` and its accessible name includes the error's message.
- [ ] A tile with no error has no `data-issue`.
- [ ] A card that both clashes with another deck and has an error shows both reasons.
- [ ] When the collection couldn't be read, no ownership marks appear, matching the editor's existing hint.
- [ ] Every new string has its `zh-CN.json` entry (`i18n.test.ts`).
- [ ] `pnpm --dir apps/web exec vitest run src/game/deckbuilder/DeckWorkshop.test.tsx`, typecheck and eslint pass.

## Size and risks
Small: three files and a test. A tile's accessible name grows for a card in error, so a test that finds tiles by name may need its expected text updated. Test ids stay as they are.

```

pnpm --dir apps/web exec vitest run src/game/deckbuilder/DeckWorkshop.test.tsx src/game/deckbuilder/browse.test.tsx src/game/deckbuilder/savedBrowse.test.tsx src/i18n/i18n.test.ts
pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck
pnpm exec eslint apps/web/src/game/deckbuilder apps/web/src/i18n
```

## Done when

- [ ] An unowned card's tile has `data-issue="L5"` and the L5 sentence in its accessible name and `title` (test 1).
- [ ] A tile with no error has no `data-issue`, no `title` and no flag (test 1).
- [ ] The first error naming a card wins (test 2).
- [ ] A tile with both a clash and an error gives both reasons, with one flag (test 3).
- [ ] With `collection: null` there is no L5 mark and the hint shows (test 4).
- [ ] The three new strings are in `zh-CN.json`, and `i18n.test.ts` passes.
- [ ] The four commands above pass. So do the harness's web tests and `cargo fmt --check`. Nothing in `crates/` changes, so the cargo checks, `spec check` and `patches check` stay as they are on `main`.

## Risks

- **Hidden information (rule 7):** the tile shows only the validator's existing verdict; it reads no new data.
- **i18n patterns:** each new key has at least two words of its own, so `t()` may try it as a pattern on other sentences. None of the engine's or the server's sentences has their shape, and the tokens match in English and Chinese (the `i18n.test.ts` token check).
- **The tile's `aria-label`:** it grows only on a tile in error. No test or e2e spec finds a tile by its accessible name: tests use test ids, and B38's deck has no per-card error.
- **CSS:** the B30 test in `browse.test.tsx` forbids sticky or fixed positioning, and the new rules add neither. The button rule keeps the `.deckbuilder.app-shell` scope.
- **Conflicts:** no open pull request touching these files is known, but the planner has no GitHub access to check.

## Open questions

None block the build. These decisions were made here and a person may change them:
- **Wording:** the `aria-label` is `"Remove X from D: <sentence>"`, and when both apply the `title` is `"Also in D. <sentence>"`. The other option was joining the two with a newline and adding no new strings; it was rejected because a sentence built from untranslated pieces reads badly in Chinese.
- **Tone:** an issue tile gets an amber edge and amber flag (`#e0a93b`, the verdict's hint dot). A tile in both keeps R251's red edge. The other option was red for an issue; it was rejected because the editor's verdict is a hint, not an alarm (`deckbuilder.css`, "verdicts").
- **Placement:** the map is a `useMemo` in `DeckEditor`, as the issue proposes, not a new `workshop.ts` helper.

## Goal

In the deck editor, each deck-list tile for a card that the validator's verdict names (L3, L5, L6, L7) gets three things:
- a `data-issue="<rule>"` attribute;
- the validator's translated sentence in its `title` and `aria-label`;
- the existing `db-tile-flag` mark, in the verdict's amber.

A card that also clashes with a compared deck gives both reasons. Errors with no `cardId` (L2) stay only in the verdict box. With no collection, `deckVerdict` already treats every card as owned (`ownershipUnknown`, `apps/web/src/game/deckbuilder/workshop.ts:87-105`), so no L5 mark can appear. Every new string gets a `zh-CN.json` entry. The client only shows what the validator decided (CLAUDE.md rule 7).
